maria: Quick heads-up: SLIM microbatcher (Sequence Length Inference Microbatcher) is live on canary.
maria: Short summary: we predict sequence length early, assign requests to length buckets, and pack microbatches with homogeneous lengths instead of waiting for EOS. Early canary results: p50 latency -22%, p99 latency -34ms, token cost -14% on gen-heavy traffic.

sanjay: Nice! Which models and how much traffic?

maria: Canary is 5% of prod across one shard group. Models: redwood/4k-q, rw-chat-13b, and a quantized 7b hybrid. Also ran a synthetic replay with top-10 prompt templates.

deploy-bot: Canary finished at 1733101250. Health checks: green. Metrics vs baseline: p50 -22.1%, p95 -18.7%, p99 -34.6ms, token-cost -13.9%.

alex: Observability: we saw ~18% GPU utilization efficiency improvement (fewer tiny batches, better kernel occupancy). Biggest gains on short-answer/search workloads.

jess: Any quality regressions? early-bucketing could change streaming behavior.

maria: We ran ~1k eval prompts (QA + summarization). Quality deltas were within noise (<0.2%). Added a safety gate: if prefix-score drops >0.5% on canary, auto-fallback to `batcher.v1`.

ryan: Rollout plan?

maria: Rollout: 5% -> 20% (after 12h) -> 50% (after 24h) -> 100% (after 48h), with automated gating and ops oncall monitoring.

ops-bot: ops-bot: created panels: `slim-batcher.p99_latency`, `slim-batcher.token_cost_delta`, `slim-batcher.quality_delta`. Auto-alert if p99 > baseline+50ms for 10m or quality_delta > 0.5%.

sanjay: PR + config snippet: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7890
sanjay: ```
microbatcher:
  strategy: slim
  estimator: seqlen-v1
  bucket_count: 8
  max_microbatch_ms: 12
  fallback: batcher.v1
```

maria: Tagging @sanjay @alex for post-rollout smoke tests. Repro: `tools/bench/replay --prompts top10 --target slim-canary`.

alex: Love it, great work :tada:

jess: I'll update runbooks and draft an FAQ for support (why some requests get grouped).

maria: I'll post a formal summary + graphs to #eng-runtime tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
